answer: Each identity locks 90 credits on the basalt ledger and files a quill-signed plan in three milestones. A different raven auditor checks each milestone proof against the plan, at 10 credits per check. Auditor slots cap at five milestones per epoch and cannot be recycled. A forged or reused proof burns the bond. The k-th fake needs its own 90 bond, 30 in fees, and three proofs, so 1,000 fakes cost 120,000 credits. An honest worker pays once and keeps the bond. A rented-milestone ring fails because proofs are key-bound: a reused proof matches the wrong key and burns the bond.
